claims.text: High configurational entropy in noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles ensures a homogeneous atomic distribution.
A homogeneous atomic distribution induces a uniform surface strain.
Uniform surface strain tunes adsorption energies at catalytic sites.
Entropy-driven stabilization produces more reliable nanoparticle formation than in conventional binary or ternary alloys.
Entropy-driven stabilization enhances catalytic performance relative to conventional binary or ternary alloys.
The initial nanoparticle precursors contain five or more noble metals randomly distributed in an alloy lattice.
HEA nanoparticles are predicted to have more uniform atomic dispersion than binary or ternary alloy nanoparticles synthesized under the same conditions.
HEA nanoparticles are predicted to have a narrower distribution of surface strains than binary or ternary alloy nanoparticles.
High mixing entropy prevents metal segregation.
Suppression of segregation yields a homogeneous alloy structure.
Structural homogeneity minimizes localized strain variations.
Consistent surface strain modulates surface electronic properties.
Strain-mediated changes in surface electronic properties optimize adsorption energies of catalytic intermediates.
HEA nanoparticles will exhibit higher turnover frequency than binary or ternary alloy nanoparticles synthesized under identical conditions.
HEA nanoparticles will exhibit greater operational durability than binary or ternary alloy nanoparticles.
The activity and durability improvements arise from uniform surface strain altering reaction energetics.
The proposed mechanism applies to noble metal–based nanoparticles containing at least five principal elements.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to particles typically 5–15 nm in size.
The proposed mechanism applies under controlled thermal and reducing synthesis environments and moderate reaction conditions.
Post-synthesis annealing promotes segregation, which should reduce structural uniformity and catalytic activity.
